la:adj:intactus.html:
in-tactus, a, um, adj.,
untouched, uninjured, intact.
Lit.: cervix juvencae,not broken to the yoke,: grex,: boves,: nix,: exercitus integer intactusque,: intactum aliquem inviolatumque dimittere,: integri intactique fugerunt,; : ferro corpus,: bello fines,: vulnere miles,: arx bellis,: corpus ab vexatione,: intactus profugit,: Britannus,unsubdued,: Scythae perpetuo ab alieno imperio intacti, aut invicti,: fides,unstained,: vires,unimpaired,: intactus superstitione,free from superstition,: vir haud intacti religione animi,: intactus infamiā,of spotless integrity,: intacta invidiā media,: (triarii) per alios manipulos prope intacti evasere,: caput intactum buxo,. —
Transf.
Untried, unattempted: prorsus nihil intactum, neque quietum pati,; cf. bellum,without combat,fin.: novā intactāque ratione,: Dryadum silvas saltusque sequamur Intactos,: carmen,: thensauros Proserpinae intactos ad eam diem spoliavit,; cf.: sacrilegas admovere manus intactis illis thensauris,: intactis opulentior thesauris Arabum,.—Of a play not yet acted: esurit (Statius) intactam Paridi nisi vendat Agaven,; cf.: intactum dicere carmen,: intacta carmina

discens, .—

Untouched, undefiled, chaste, of virgins: Pallas,: cui pater intactam dederat,: virgo,: intactior omni Sabina,; cf.: utinam publica saltem his intacta malis agerentur sacra,not disgraced by these scandals,.
